patches.rationale: The issue requires is_expired to treat the exact boundary inserted_at + ttl as expired (non-strict comparison), including zero TTL. Currently it uses strict '>' which keeps entries alive at the boundary. Change to '>=' to make now == inserted_at + ttl expired, while preserving strict-before (False) and strict-after (True). Add a new regression test file covering boundary, zero TTL, before, and after cases, plus type checks.

edits.old:
def is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now):
    return now > inserted_at + ttl
edits.new:
def is_expired(inserted_at, ttl, now):
    return now >= inserted_at + ttl

contract_tests: tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_expired_exactly_at_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 15) is True (now == inserted_at + ttl).
tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_zero_ttl_expires_at_insertion_instant asserts is_expired(10, 0, 10) is True (ttl == 0, now == inserted_at).
tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_not_expired_strictly_before_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 14) is False (now < inserted_at + ttl).
tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_expired_strictly_after_boundary asserts is_expired(10, 5, 16) is True (now > inserted_at + ttl).
tests/test_cache_expiry.py::test_is_expired_returns_bool asserts isinstance(..., bool) for boundary, before, and zero-ttl cases, confirming return type unchanged.
